mission: Anthropic's team says it 'studies how large language models work internally as a foundation for AI safety.' The goal is to explain model behaviour from the inside, so problems that are hard to see from outside, such as stated reasoning that differs from what the model is really doing, can be detected. Early work mapped mechanisms; newer work applies the methods to real Claude models.

key_work.title: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning
key_work.plain_summary: Showed that 'sparse autoencoders' can split a small model's tangled neurons into thousands of cleaner, human-readable features.

key_work.title: Mapping the Mind of a Large Language Model (Scaling Monosemanticity)
key_work.plain_summary: Scaled the same method to Claude 3 Sonnet, finding millions of features (e.g. for the Golden Gate Bridge, deception, bias) that could be turned up or down.

key_work.title: Tracing the thoughts of a large language model (circuit tracing / 'Biology of an LLM')
key_work.plain_summary: 'Attribution graphs' trace step by step how Claude reaches an answer, revealing planning ahead in poems and cases where its explanation did not match its real computation.

key_work.title: Open-sourcing circuit tracing tools
key_work.plain_summary: Released the circuit-tracing tooling so outside researchers can make attribution graphs for open models.

key_work.title: Signs of introspection in large language models
key_work.plain_summary: Tested whether Claude can notice concepts injected into its own activations; found limited, unreliable but real signs of introspective awareness.

key_work.title: Natural Language Autoencoders: Turning Claude's thoughts into text
key_work.plain_summary: 'AI models like Claude talk in words but think in numbers' — this study trains Claude to translate its internal activations into readable text.

key_work.title: A global workspace in language models
key_work.plain_summary: Reports evidence of an emergent shared 'mental workspace' inside language models where information is broadcast for use across the network.

warnings.text: It is hard to reason about the safety of neural networks without understanding what happens inside them (team page).
A model's stated reasoning can differ from what it is actually doing internally, so explanations cannot simply be trusted.
Current interpretability only explains part of a model's computation; much remains a black box (stated limitation across circuit papers).

recommendations.text: Use interpretability to detect unsafe behaviour or dishonest reasoning and safeguard against it, including in pre-deployment audits (team page; RSP auditing work).
Make interpretability tools open so the wider research community can inspect models (open-sourced circuit tracing).
Treat interpretability as one layer of evidence alongside behavioural evaluations and monitoring, consistent with Anthropic's RSP risk reports.
